The moonj products of Amethi exude an earthy elegance, their natural hues and textures a testament to the beauty of simplicity. From stunning baskets to intricate mats and wall hangings, each piece is a labor of love. Admired by connoisseurs of eco-friendly and sustainable products, these handcrafted creations bring a touch of rustic charm to any space they adorn.

With its deep, lustrous ebony hue and intricate motifs etched into its smooth surface, the enigmatic black pottery of Azamgarh, Uttar Pradesh is a true masterpiece of artistry. From delicate tea sets to ornate vases and decorative figurines, each piece is a unique and stunning work of art. The tactile quality of the pottery, combined with the ethereal designs, creates a sensory experience that is truly unforgettable.

The handicrafts techniques from Bahraich, Uttar Pradesh, are a masterful display of the region's ingenuity and resourcefulness. The artisans of Bahraich have long been known for their exquisite handcrafted products made from wheat stalks, which are expertly woven and shaped into stunning baskets, mats, and decorative items.

The Bindi (Tikuli) from Ballia is a popular ornamental handicraft that has a widespread cultural significance and is worn by many. Available in a variety of designs, colours and shapes, the Bindi can be applied to the forehead as a beauty mark and accentuates the facial features of the wearer.

The skilled artisans of Banda transform raw blocks of stone into stunning works of art, from exquisite sculptures and ornate jewellery to stunning home decor items, using traditional techniques that have been honed over centuries. Each piece is unique and beautiful, featuring intricate designs that are both elegant and timeless. The use of high-quality natural stones, combined with the artisans' deft hands and keen eye for detail, creates a product of unparalleled quality and beauty.

Nestled in Uttar Pradesh's cultural hub, Bareilly, Zari and Zardozi craftsmanship mesmerize with their intricate beauty. Handcrafted by skilled artisans, these embellishments adorn fabrics, lending an aura of opulence to traditional attire. Rooted in centuries-old tradition, each stitch narrates a tale of heritage and craftsmanship. Bareilly's Zari and Zardozi industry not only preserves artistic legacies but also provides livelihoods, enriching communities through timeless artistry.

Bareilly, in Uttar Pradesh, is renowned for its handcrafted bamboo products, known for their natural beauty and eco-friendliness. Using traditional techniques, local artisans create a variety of items, including furniture, tableware, and decorative pieces, all from organically grown bamboo.

In the heart of Uttar Pradesh's Bareilly, the Goldsmith industry shines as a beacon of craftsmanship and tradition. Here, skilled artisans meticulously mold precious metals into exquisite jewelry pieces, each reflecting timeless elegance and intricate designs. Rooted in cultural heritage, this industry not only symbolizes prosperity but also sustains generations of artisanal expertise, contributing to the region's rich legacy of craftsmanship and artistic finesse.

Handcrafted wooden products from Basti, Uttar Pradesh, are known for their intricate designs and use of local Sheesham wood. Artisans, using generations-old techniques, craft beautiful and durable furniture, decorative items, and toys.

Bhadohi's carpets, also known as Bhadohi rugs or Bhadohi carpets, are renowned for their exceptional craftsmanship and artistic designs. The weavers in Bhadohi employ traditional techniques handed down through generations to create carpets that are truly works of art. These carpets feature a wide range of patterns, from intricate floral motifs to geometric designs, and are available in various sizes and colors. With their soft texture, durability, and timeless appeal, Bhadohi carpets have become sought-after decorative pieces, cherished by homeowners and collectors around the world.

The wooden crafts of Bijnor are not just decorative but also functional, with each piece designed to last a lifetime, a true heirloom that can be passed down through generations. The use of sustainable and eco-friendly materials in these crafts makes them not just beautiful but also responsible choices for any home. The natural grains and patterns of the wood lend a unique texture and depth to each piece, making them one-of-a-kind creations that are sure to stand out.

Budaun district in Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its exquisite zari and zardozi embroidery. Zari embroidery utilizes metallic threads, often made of gold or silver, to create intricate designs on fabrics. Zardozi, a more elaborate form, incorporates gold and silver wires, silk, and metallic threads. Skilled artisans in Budaun showcase exceptional craftsmanship, creating stunning designs that adorn traditional Indian garments. The labor-intensive and time-consuming process of zari and zardozi embroidery makes each piece a true work of art.

From exquisitely designed crockery to charming home decor, the ceramic products of Bulandshahar exude an unmatched warmth and character. The use of high-quality materials and eco-friendly techniques in these crafts makes them not just beautiful but also responsible choices for any home. With each piece telling a unique story of the region's rich cultural tapestry, the ceramic products of Bulandshahar are a true testament to the human spirit and the pursuit of excellence

Chandauli district in Uttar Pradesh is known for its intricate zari and zardozi embroidery work. Zari Zardozi involves the use of metallic thread, usually gold or silver, to create intricate designs on fabric. The embroidery work of Chandauli is famous for its intricate designs and is often used to embellish traditional Indian attire such as sarees, salwar kameez, and lehengas.

Product: Wooden Toys and Wood Art Products
Description: Whether used as decor or as playthings, Chitrakoot's wooden toys are lovingly crafted by hand using the finest quality wood, resulting in a product that is not only aesthetically pleasing but also durable and long-lasting. From traditional figurines to modern designs, these toys are infused with a sense of wonder and playfulness that appeals to people of all ages.

Deoria district in Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its diverse range of decorative products. Skilled artisans in Deoria employ traditional techniques to create exquisite decorative items like wall hangings, table runners, and cushion covers.

Product: Ankle Bells (Ghungroo), Bells and Brass Products
Description: Etah district in Uttar Pradesh is famous for its production of ankle bells (Ghungroo), brass bells, and a wide range of brass products. The ankle bells, made from brass, produce a melodious sound when worn by classical Indian dancers, making them highly coveted in the dance community. Skilled artisans in Etah create brass bells of various sizes and designs, which are widely used for religious, decorative, and musical purposes. Additionally, they craft an array of brass products, including decorative items, utensils, and household items, using traditional techniques.

Farukhabad's zari zardosi is an intricate embroidery renowned for its delicate gold and silver threads meticulously hand-stitched onto fabric. Artisans, using techniques passed down through generations, weave beautiful floral and geometric patterns, creating stunning embellishments for clothing, accessories, and home furnishings.

The jute wall hangings from Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh are a stunning embodiment of the natural beauty and craftsmanship that India is renowned for. Made with the finest quality jute fibers, each piece is meticulously woven by skilled artisans, resulting in a work of art that is both intricate and captivating. From earthy tones to vibrant hues, these wall hangings showcase a wide array of colors and designs, each one more stunning than the last.

Gorakhpur district in Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its handicrafts, particularly terracotta products and readymade garments. Skilled artisans in Gorakhpur create pottery, figurines, and decorative items using locally sourced clay. These unique creations are molded and baked in kilns for durability. The district also offers a diverse selection of readymade garments, featuring traditional and modern designs, predominantly using cotton and silk fabrics. Gorakhpur's fashion styles range from sarees and salwar kameez to western wear, showcasing a wide variety of choices.

Jalaun district in Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its exquisite handmade paper art. Skilled artisans use locally sourced natural fibers to create intricate designs, including flowers, birds, and nature-inspired motifs. Techniques like embossing, painting, and printing are employed to bring these artworks to life. The range of finished products includes journals, greeting cards, bookmarks, and decorative wall hangings. Not only visually appealing, but Jalaun's handmade paper art is also environmentally friendly, being crafted with sustainable materials and techniques.

Jaunpur district in Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its exquisite woollen carpets, locally known as Dari. Skilled artisans hand-weave these carpets using high-quality wool sourced from local sheep. The carpets boast intricate floral motifs, geometric patterns, and even calligraphy. Known for their soft texture, durability, and vibrant colors achieved through natural dyes, Jaunpur's Dari carpets are available in various sizes, catering to different spaces. This traditional craft has been thriving in Jaunpur for centuries, captivating both local and international markets.

The leather industry in Kanpur Nagar has a rich history, and it is a hub for leather production, supplying high-quality products to customers across India and beyond. Whether it's a pair of sturdy boots or a stylish handbag, the leather products from Kanpur Nagar are known for their intricate designs and attention to detail. The leather used in Kanpur Nagar is unique, of high quality, and durable.

Kasganj district in Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its exquisite Zari Zardozi work. This intricate embroidery art form involves the use of metallic wires, silk threads, and other materials to create stunning designs on fabrics like silk, velvet, and cotton. Traditional floral patterns, peacock motifs, and cultural designs are common in Kasganj's Zari Zardozi work. Skilled artisans employ techniques such as hand stitching, weaving, and knotting to achieve impeccable craftsmanship. The finished products often feature embellishments like sequins, beads, and decorative elements, adding an extra touch of elegance.

Product: Banana Fiber Products and Banana Products
Description: Kushinagar district in Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its banana fiber products and banana-based items. The abundant banana cultivation in the region has led to the development of unique artisanal skills using various parts of the banana plant. The stem of the banana plant yields strong and durable banana fiber, which is skillfully crafted into bags, mats, and baskets, known for their beauty and quality. Kushinagar also produces delicious banana chips, banana jam, and banana candy, made from carefully selected bananas using traditional techniques, ensuring exceptional quality in the final products.

In the verdant landscapes of Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, Tribal Craft thrives as a testament to indigenous artistry. Honoring centuries-old traditions, skilled artisans create exquisite handcrafted items reflecting tribal motifs and cultural heritage. From intricately carved wooden artifacts to vibrant textiles adorned with traditional designs, each piece encapsulates the essence of tribal life.

The gaura stone craft from Mahoba, Uttar Pradesh is a breathtaking showcase of India's architectural and sculptural prowess. Made from the finest quality sandstone, each piece is a true masterpiece, featuring intricate carvings and unique designs that are a testament to the skill and dedication of the artisans. From traditional temples to modern-day sculptures, these creations are both timeless and contemporary, reflecting India's rich cultural heritage and artistic vision.

Tarkashi art is a traditional form of metal wire inlay work that originated in Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh. It involves the use of fine metallic wires that are carefully inlaid into intricate designs on a variety of surfaces, including wood, brass, and copper. The art form is known for its intricate and delicate patterns, often depicting scenes from nature and daily life. Whether it's a decorative box or a piece of furniture, tarkashi art adds an elegant and sophisticated touch to any space.

Mainpuri's Zari Zardosi is an embroidery known for its intricate beauty. Skilled artisans weave delicate threads of gold and silver into mesmerizing floral and geometric patterns, adorning fabrics like garments, wall hangings, and more. This heritage craft, passed down through generations, is admired for its meticulous detailing and captivating designs.

Handcrafted in Mathura, Uttar Pradesh, these exquisite costumes adorn deities like Thakurji. Crafted from fine silk or cotton, they come in vibrant colors and are embellished with intricate zari work, using gold and silver threads. These traditional ensembles reflect the region's rich cultural heritage and craftsmanship.

Crafted from local red soapstone, these sculptures depict diverse subjects, from Hindu deities to everyday life. Skilled artisans meticulously carve intricate details, bringing the stone to life. Exquisite necklaces, meticulously woven with silk and zari threads. Often adorned with intricate beadwork and semi-precious stones, these necklaces embody Mathura's rich cultural heritage.

Nestled in the heart of Uttar Pradesh, Mirzapur's brass work shines as a beacon of craftsmanship and tradition. Here, skilled artisans meticulously mold brass into exquisite artifacts, each reflecting timeless elegance and intricate designs. Rooted in centuries-old tradition, this industry not only symbolizes prosperity but also sustains generations of artisanal expertise, contributing to the region's rich legacy of craftsmanship and artistic finesse.

Pilibhit district in Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its traditional wooden products and the exquisite art of bamboo flute making. Skilled artisans meticulously handcraft bamboo flutes that produce rich and melodious sounds, captivating musicians and music enthusiasts. These flutes are integral to traditional Indian music. Additionally, Pilibhit is celebrated for its locally sourced wooden products, including furniture, utensils, and toys, which boast durability and intricate designs, showcasing the region's exceptional craftsmanship.

Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh is famous for its exquisite moonj products, with a range of styles and sizes available to suit different needs and preferences. The artisans of Prayagraj use their expert knowledge and skills to craft baskets, mats, and other household items. Mats for sleeping and sitting, as well as decorative items such as lampshades and wall hangings are also created.

There is a considerable amount of wood-related work in the district of Raebareli. Wood crafting is done by means of a cutting tool resulting in a wooden figure or figurine, or in the sculptural ornamentation of a wooden object. The items manufactured here include household items such as doors, charms, beds, and artistic works such as wooden toys and artwork. The raw material required for wood-work is available locally.

Product: Applique Work along with Patch Work,Zari Patch work, and Mentha
Description: Rampur district in Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its captivating applique work, patchwork, and zari patchwork. Skilled artisans meticulously cut and stitch colored fabric onto a base fabric, creating mesmerizing designs. Patchwork involves stitching together small fabric pieces to form larger designs, often with contrasting colors. Zari patchwork utilizes metallic thread, resulting in elaborate and shiny patterns. Additionally, Rampur is a significant producer of mentha oil, extracted from mentha plant leaves, widely utilized in the pharmaceutical and food industries.

Wood craft, which is the main handicraft of this district, is about 400 years old. These products are famous for their beautiful and intricate designs and carvings. Sheesham wood is the main raw material used in this industry. The export of wood carving furniture and handicraft products to various countries is carried out by exporting units in the district.

Sambhal district in Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its unique handicrafts made from horn and bone. The process of making these handicrafts involves skilled craftsmanship and a great deal of patience. Sambhal offers a wide range of decorative horn-bone handicrafts available in different attractive looks, designs and patterns. Indeed artisans of Sambhal are known worldwide for making a spell-bound range of decorative items that are popular in not only national but also in international markets.

There are several types of brassware craft that are popular in Sant Kabir Nagar, each with its distinct style and flair. One such type is the exquisite brass utensils that feature intricate patterns and designs, often depicting mythological scenes and motifs.Another type is the ornate brass lamps and candle holders that are crafted with painstaking attention to detail, creating a warm and inviting ambiance in any room.

Zari embroidery involves the use of gold or silver metallic thread to create intricate patterns and designs on fabric. On the other hand, Zardozi embroidery is a more complex form of embroidery that involves the use of gold, silver, and copper wires, as well as precious stones, sequins, and beads, to create intricate and detailed designs on fabric.This technique is typically used to create stunning embellishments on traditional Indian garments such as sarees, lehengas, as well as on other textiles like wall hangings and tablecloths.

Product: Rim and Axle and Iron Work
Description: In the industrial heartland of Shamli, Uttar Pradesh, Rim and Axle and Iron Work thrive as symbols of precision and durability. Skilled artisans meticulously craft sturdy rims and axles, ensuring reliability and safety for various vehicles. Rooted in a legacy of craftsmanship, Shamli's ironworkers combine traditional techniques with modern innovations, catering to diverse transportation needs while contributing to the region's industrial prowess and economic growth.

Shravasti, Uttar Pradesh is home to several indigenous tribes that have a rich cultural heritage of traditional crafts, that reflect their deep connection to nature and their ancestral traditions. Some of the most popular tribal crafts from Shravasti include bamboo crafts, which are created using bamboo reeds and are used to make baskets, mats, and other household items. Another popular craft is pottery, where clay is shaped and fired to create beautiful and functional vessels for cooking, storing, and serving food.

Moonj products are a popular handicraft of Sultanpur district in Uttar Pradesh. Moonj is a type of grass that is native to the region and is used to make a variety of products, such as baskets, mats, and bags. The process of making these products involves weaving the moonj strands together to create intricate patterns and designs. The products are known for their durability and are widely used for household and storage purposes.

Unnao's Zari Zardosi are textiles known for their intricate gold and silver threadwork, meticulously hand-embroidered onto silk or satin fabrics. Artisans from the region use generations-old techniques to create these luxurious garments and accessories, often adorned with floral or geometric patterns.

Unnao's leather products are known for their intricate hand-stitching and vegetable tanning techniques. Crafted from locally sourced hides, these products are imbued with a timeless quality and natural beauty. Each piece is unique, showcasing the artisan's skill and the inherent variations of the leather.

Gulabi Meenakari from Varanasi are exquisite artworks created by fusing colored glass onto a metal base. Each piece showcases vibrant floral and geometric motifs, or even scenes inspired by mythology and daily life. The meticulous craftsmanship and unique rose pink color ("Gulabi" in Hindi) make these intricate enameled creations truly special.

Varanasi's wooden lacquerware, known for its vibrant hues, intricate designs, and smooth finish, is a unique art form. Crafted from wood, these decorative items are coated in layers of lac, a natural resin, and hand-painted with scenes depicting local flora, fauna, and religious themes. The lac not only enhances their beauty but also protects them from wear and tear.

Varanasi, a city known for its rich history and cultural heritage, is also home to a unique tradition of handcrafted wooden toys. Made by skilled artisans, these vibrant toys are more than just playthings; they are miniature works of art, often featuring intricate designs and natural lacquers. Each toy is a testament to the craftsmanship and artistic legacy passed down through generations in Varanasi.

Bageshwar is a town in Uttarakhand, India known for its rich tradition of copper craftsmanship. The town produces a range of copper-based products, including kitchenware, utensils, and decorative items. The craft of copper ware is an age old, highly skilled craft that has been passed down from one generation to its next.

Nainital is known for its range of products featuring the traditional art form of Aipan, including home decor, clothing, and accessories. Aipan is a type of hand-painted design that is traditionally used for special events and ceremonies, that is said to invoke a divine power which brings good fortune and deters evil.

Rudraprayagis is known for its rich heritage and temple architecture, with the production of woodcraft temple imitations being a major attraction. They are often bought as gifts and souvenirs by devotees and tourists alike and are carved by skilled craftspersons.

Udham Singh Nagar in Uttarakhand produces a range of products made from Moonj grass, including baskets, mats, and other decorative items. These products are produced by skilled artisans and showcase a variety of intricate woven patterns and colours.

Alipurduar Wooden Furniture is a range of beautifully crafted, high-quality wooden furniture made in Alipurduar, a town in the Indian state of West Bengal. The collection includes a variety of pieces, such as tables, chairs, sofas, beds, and storage units, in a range of styles to suit any home or office.

Bankura district produces a number of terracotta handicrafts, the most popular being the Bankura horse which is the Logo of All India Handicrafts. It has been internationally commended for its elegance and unique charm and is hand-crafted by skilled artisans using techniques passed down through generations. Originally used for village rituals, it now adorns drawing rooms across the world as symbols of Indian folk-art.

Dokra is a type of traditional, handmade metal casting made in the Bankura district. Dokra artisans use the lost-wax casting method to create intricate, detailed pieces using brass, bronze, or copper. The finished products are often intricate, decorative figurines and other items, such as jewelry, lamps, and ornaments. The Dokra is known for its high quality and attention to detail, and is prized by collectors and art enthusiasts alike.

Santiniketan is known for its range of high-quality leather products. The products are made using high quality sustainable leather. The craftsmen of the villages were trained under the Rural Development Programme of Visva-Bharati University at Santiniketan. The range includes a variety of leather goods, such as bags, wallets, belts, and other accessories. The material used is vegetable tanned leather with art work done by touch dyeing.Its artistic leather bags are popular in foreign markets and are exported to many countries around Europe and the US.

Sital Pati is a type of traditional, handwoven mat made using natural fibers such as grass, straw, cane or murta plants. Among the areas of Cooch Behar where Sitalpatis are woven, Sagareswar, Ghugumari and Pashnadanga are important centres. Mats with decorative designs are called nakshi pati. UNESCO has recognised the Traditional Art of Shital Pati weaving of Sylhet and included it in the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

The masks and wall hangings are hand-carved by skilled artisans using techniques passed down through generations. The wood pieces are kept submerged in large reservoirs containing mulberry gum powder, bleaching powder and sal and are taken out after a week and sun-dried. Various timber varieties such as Gamari, Sal, Mango, Pakur, and Mahogany are used. The wooden masks are meant for use in Gambheera dances or Palas (musical folk theaters), as the carvers, or the performers, treat each mask philosophically, by considering it as the Mukha (face), rather than a Mukhosh (mask) – the belief being that it comes alive as soon as one puts his face behind it.

Bamboo craft from Dakshin Dinajpur is one type of traditional handicraft made into many products including such as home decor, or as functional items, such as baskets or furniture. Basketry weaving is the primary source of livelihood of the community in the district. The crafts are made by skilled artisans using techniques passed down through generations, and are known for their durability, versatility, and attention to detail. The finished products are often used for decorative purposes.

Costume or fashion jewelry includes a range of decorative items that are manufactured as less expensive ornamentation to complement a particular fashionable outfit or garment as opposed to "real" or "fine" jewelry,. This type of jewelry has paralleled the styles of its more precious counterparts and Hooghly has a range of offerings made of inexpensive simulated gemstones, such as rhinestones or lucite, set in pewter, silver, nickel, or brass.

Howrah ornaments are made up of gold and precious stones and just like the rituals and customs of Bengal, it imbibes beauty, traditions and modernity beautifully. The traditional jewellery comprises of a pati haar which is a heavy studded necklace; Jhumko is a pair of intricately designed earrings which usually have beautiful floral motifs and Nath or the nose ring is like the traditional variety used in India. The Chur, which can sometimes weigh upto 50 grams is the traditional gold bangle of West Bengal, is made entirely of pure gold, and is one of the most exquisite items.

Wood carving from Jalpaiguri is a traditional art form that is known for its intricate and detailed designs that are carved using various types of wood using chisels and hammers. The carvings are often used to decorate furniture, temples, and other architectural structures, and they depict a wide range of subjects, including religious and mythological figures, animals, and abstract patterns. The wood carving tradition of Jalpaiguri is an important part of the region's cultural heritage and is still practiced by a majority of artisans today.

Sal leaf products are a type of traditional handicraft made using the leaves of the sal tree, which is native to the Indian subcontinent. The leaves are collected and dried before being used to create a variety of items, such as baskets, bowls, trays, and other decorative and functional items. Sal leaf products are known for their durability, versatility, and natural, rustic beauty, and are often used for decorative purposes or as part of traditional festivals and celebrations in Jhargram, West Bengal.

Sabai grass-based handicraft is a type of traditional craft made using the leaves of the sabai grass plant, which is native to the Indian subcontinent. The leaves are collected, dried, and woven into a variety of items, both decorative and functional in nature. Mostly found in the north Jhargram region, the thin and long fibrous leaves of Sabai Grass, which are flexible with high strength are utilized to produce Sabai grass rope. A wide range of rope based utility items like mats, foot mats, serving trays, flower vase holders, bowels, baskets, boxes and other decorative items are made from sabai grass.

Kolkata, the capital city of West Bengal, is known for its Leather Goods. The products are made using locally sourced, sustainable leather and are known for their durability, style, and craftmanship. The range includes a variety of leather goods, such as bags, wallets, belts, and other accessories. Brisul Haat, Entaly, Bagree and Barabazar are some of the famous markets which have a variety of Leather products.

Clay Dolls made in the Ghurni village of Nadia are a type of traditional handicraft made in Krishnanagar region. The King of Krishnanagar was a great patron of the fine arts, including literature and music and supported the production of clay dolls. The creations of these artists are displayed in many of the handicraft museums and art galleries of the world. In India, we have a large display of these dolls in the Shankar’s Doll Museum in New Delhi.

North Twenty Four Parganas district has high quality Jute products having many uses which are popular for their rustic beauty. All of these are made using locally sourced materials. The collection includes a variety of product made by the local such as bags, baskets, mats, and other decorative home decor items.

North Twenty Four Parganas is known for jewel boxes, used for storing valuable personal items such as jewelry, watches, and other trinkets. Jewelry boxes can be made from a variety of materials such as wood, leather, and metal, and they often feature decorative elements such as inlaid designs, engravings, and hardware. They can be found in many different styles and sizes, from small portable boxes to large, ornate armoires.

Paschim Medinipur is known for Patachitra which is a type of hand-painted scroll painting made using natural dyes and pigments on cloth or paper. These usually depict a variety of subjects, including mythology, folklore, and contemporary themes. Patachitra artisans are known for their skill and attention to detail, and the finished paintings are often vibrant, intricate works of traditional art.

Madur is a form of traditional mat made by fiber that is obtained from the leaves of the madur plant, which is native to India. Mat products are made from this fiber and can include items such as baskets, bags, and other household items. Madur is a strong and durable fiber and its mat products hence are known for their durability and practicality. The production of madur and mat products is an important industry in the state and these products are made by artisans in Paschim Medinipur.

The Dokra technique of metal casting is practiced in the Purba Bardhaman district. Dokra artisans use the lost-wax casting method to create intricate, detailed pieces using brass, bronze, or copper. The finished products are often intricate, decorative figurines and other items, such as jewelry, lamps, and ornaments. West Bengal Dokra is known for its high quality and attention to detail, and is prized by collectors and art enthusiasts alike.

Patachitra is a type of traditional, hand-painted scroll painting made in the Indian state of West Bengal. The paintings are created using natural dyes and pigments on cloth or paper, and depict a variety of subjects, including mythology, folklore, and contemporary themes. Patachitra artisans are known for their skill and attention to detail, and the finished paintings are often vibrant, intricate works of art.

Purulia district is known for Lac, which is a natural resin produced by certain insects, and lac products are made from this resin. These products can include items such as beads, bangles, and other jewelry, as well as decorative objects and other household items. Lac products from Purulia are made by artisans in the region using traditional techniques.

Purulia Chau Masks are traditional masks that are used in various dance forms, including the Chhau dance, which is a popular folk dance in the region. These masks are hand-crafted using a variety of materials, such as paper mache, clay, and paint. They are highly decorative and feature intricate designs, and bright colors.

These goods from South 24 Parganas are made using leather, a material that is made from the hides of animals. These goods may include items such as clothing, bags, shoes, and other accessories. Leather goods from South 24 Parganas are made by artisans in the region using traditional techniques and may feature intricate designs and craftsmanship.

Jute is a natural fiber that is obtained from the stem and outer skin of the jute plant, and jute products are made from this fiber. These products are made in Uttar Dinajpur and include items such as bags, baskets, rugs, and other household items. Jute is a sustainable and renewable resource, and jute products are often biodegradable and environment friendly, hence extremely sought after.
